notes.meaning: David escaped from Naioth while Saul was incapacitated and secretly returned to Gibeah to find Jonathan. He asked Jonathan what crime or sin he had committed to make Saul want to kill him, knowing in his heart that he was innocent. It is a great comfort when facing unfair treatment to know that one's conscience is clear before God.

Jonathan tried to reassure David, refusing to believe his father was secretly plotting murder. Saul normally shared all his state plans with Jonathan, so Jonathan thought Saul's past violence was only due to temporary fits of illness. He loved his father and naturally found it hard to believe Saul could act with such wickedness.

David took a solemn oath to convince Jonathan that the danger was real. He explained that Saul had deliberately hidden the plot from Jonathan to spare his feelings, knowing how close the two friends were. David warned that his life was hanging by a thread, with only a single step between him and death.

Jonathan accepted David's warning and promised to do whatever David asked to help him. Instead of arguing or brushing off his fears, Jonathan offered full and practical support. True friendship shows itself by stepping forward when a companion is in deep distress.

Israel followed a lunar calendar, where each new month began with a New Moon festival of special sacrifices and royal feasting. As the king's son-in-law and a military leader, David was expected to sit at Saul's table. Instead of attending, David asked permission to hide in the open country until the third evening.

David told Jonathan to explain his absence by saying David had rushed home to Bethlehem for an annual family sacrifice. At this time in Israel's history, large clans often gathered once a year for special worship and shared meals. This gave Jonathan a reasonable and honorable explanation to offer the king on David's behalf.

David set up this test based on how Saul would react to the news. If Saul was pleased or calm, it would show he harbored no deadly grudge, but if he flew into a rage, it would prove his murderous plan was set. A person's reaction to ordinary disappointments often reveals what is truly in their heart.

David appealed to their covenant, a sacred and binding friendship pact they had made before God. He asked Jonathan for loyal kindness, adding that if he were truly guilty of treason, Jonathan should strike him down himself rather than hand him over to Saul. David's willingness to face death proved his complete innocence.

Jonathan firmly rejected the idea that David was guilty or that he would ever betray him. He insisted that if he found out his father had decided to kill David, he would immediately warn him. True loyalty speaks up honestly to protect a friend from harm.

David asked how Jonathan would get the news to him if Saul answered harshly. If the king became suspicious, Jonathan would be closely watched and might not be able to send an ordinary messenger. It is wise to plan carefully when facing a dangerous and unpredictable situation.

Jonathan invited David out into an open field where they could talk freely. In the royal palace, Saul's servants and spies could easily overhear their conversation. Going into the quiet countryside allowed the two friends to work out their secret plan without danger.

Jonathan called upon the Lord God of Israel as his witness and made a solemn oath to sound out his father over the next two days. If Saul felt kindly toward David, Jonathan promised to send word right away. Making this promise in God's name showed Jonathan's total commitment to his friend.

Jonathan asked God to punish him severely if he failed to warn David about Saul's evil intentions and help him escape safely. He then prayed that the Lord would be with David just as He had been with Saul when Saul first became king. Jonathan humbly accepted that God had chosen David, not himself, to rule Israel.

Looking ahead to when David would sit on the throne, Jonathan asked David to show him the Lord's faithful love throughout his life so that he would not be put to death. In ancient times, a new king often executed the family members of the previous ruler to wipe out any rivals. Jonathan asked David to rule with God's mercy rather than the harsh ways of the world.

Jonathan asked that this covenant of faithful love extend to his children and descendants forever. He pleaded that David would keep this promise even after the Lord had completely defeated all of David's enemies. True godliness cares not only for today's commitments, but for the safety of generations to come.

Jonathan sealed this covenant with the entire family and future royal house of David. He called on the Lord to bring judgment on any who broke the agreement or became enemies to David. This pact joined both households together under the watchful care of God.

Jonathan had David renew his oath of friendship, driven by his deep and sincere affection for him. Jonathan loved David as much as he loved his own life. Selfless love puts another person's welfare and God's purpose above one's own earthly status.

Jonathan turned back to their practical plan, reminding David that the New Moon festival began the next day. David's usual seat at the banquet table would be noticeably empty, and Saul would certainly ask where he was. That missing seat would quickly reveal what was hidden in the king's heart.

Jonathan told David to wait for three days and then go down to the place where he had hidden during earlier trouble, beside the stone Ezel. This stone served as a well-known landmark in the area where David could stay concealed. Having a clear and familiar meeting place helps prevent mistakes in a time of crisis.

Jonathan explained that he would shoot three arrows to the side of the stone, pretending to practice target archery. This provided a natural excuse for being out in the field with a bow and arrows without arousing any suspicion at court. Godly wisdom often uses careful, quiet plans to shield the innocent from danger.

Jonathan planned to send a servant boy to collect the arrows and shout out a coded message. If he told the boy that the arrows were on this side of him, David would know that Saul was peaceful and that it was safe to return. Jonathan backed this promise with an oath by the living Lord, ensuring David had nothing to fear.
